title: Building a Simple and Versatile Illumination System for Optogenetic Experiments
protocol: Build the electrical circuit.
Turn on the smoke absorber and the soldering iron.
Add water to the wiping sponge, have the solder at hand.
Solder circuit components to the printed circuit board (PCB board) in the order shown in the supplementary panels.
Use a small amount of solder on the soldering iron tip to heat the metal of the component and the PCB board first and melt additional solder directly onto the components.
Add flux to help with soldering.
Solder jumper wires and components as per Supplementary Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 3 instructions.
Clip the PCB board onto the “helping hands”.
Insert orange [7.6 mm (0.3 inch)] wires in pinholes a1 and a3 → ground (-).
Bend terminals of inserted wires 45 degrees and add flux.
Insert yellow [12 mm (0.4 inch)] wire from pinhole a7 to power supply (+) #7.
Insert yellow wire from pinhole d2 to d6.
Solder and then trim the back of the wires.
Insert LM317T voltage regulator in specified pinholes: Adj → e5, Vout → e6, Vin → e7.
Bend the pins and add flux.
Solder the left and right terminals.
Trim the soldered left and right terminals.
Solder the middle terminal.
Trim the middle terminal.
Insert an 820 Ω resistor into pinholes for low voltage range setting.
Solder c2 → c5 connections.
Trim c2 → c5 connections after soldering.
Insert a transistor into b3–b5 for LED control by microcontroller.
Ensure correct orientation of the transistor before inserting.
Solder wire-to-wire connectors for POT, LED, microcontroller, and power source.
Determine if a “low voltage” or “high voltage” circuit is required for the desired LED.
Place the wire from a female wire-to-wire connector through hole a5 for low voltage circuit.
Twist the bare wire ends to avoid flaking out small wire hairs.
Solder an orange [7.6 mm (0.3 inch)] jumper from a29 to the ground.
Solder a female wire-to-wire connector from a30 to the power supply (+).
Solder a male wire-to-wire connector from c29 to c30.
Cut the connector off a power supply cord, expose the wires, and strip them.
Add flux to the wires prior to soldering using a flux pen.
Place a 3.18 mm shrink tube around a male wire-to-wire connector.
Place a 4.76 mm shrink tube over the power supply wire.
Twist wires from the power supply and the male wire-to-wire connector together.
Solder the twisted wires.
Place a smaller diameter shrink tube (3.18 mm) over the soldered connections.
Shrink the smaller shrink tube with a heat gun.
Place a larger diameter shrink tube (4.76 mm) over the smaller shrink tube.
Heat again to shrink the larger shrink tube.
Place a 3.18 mm shrink tube over the wires for the switch.
Twist and solder the wires of a male wire-to-wire connector.
Place a 3.18 mm shrink tube over the soldered sections.
Shrink the tube with a heat gun.
Loop the black wire from the male wire-to-wire connector around the middle terminal of the POT.
Tighten the twist using pliers.
Solder the twisted black wire to the terminal.
Repeat with the red wire connection to the terminal.
Use pliers to break the metal tab near the red arrow.
Build the microcontroller connection.
Cut off black wires from all but one female wire-to-wire connector if making a LED driver for more than one LED.
Crimp the ends of the wire-to-wire connectors.
Push the crimped ends through the rectangular connector.
Strip the wire ends (~5 mm).
Apply flux using a flux pen.
Tin the wire by heating from below and adding solder from the top.
Place flux onto the surface contact of the LED base using a flux pen.
Heat the LED base at the contact with a generous amount of solder on a large soldering tip.
Drag the solder across the contact after a few seconds of heating.
Repeat steps to heat and drag solder across the other contact.
Clip the black wire onto the cathode (contact “C+”) using hair clips.
Place a generous amount of solder onto the large soldering tip.
Press the solder down on the wire until the solder on the LED base melts.
Hold down the wire while removing the soldering iron from it.
Place a small amount of solder paste onto the pads for the LED connections.
Place the LED over the pads using forceps.
Hold the red wire on the “A+” (anode).
Clip the red wire with a hair clip.
Press the solder down onto the wire until the solder on the LED base and the solder paste under the LED melt.
Strip the LED wires and a male wire-to-wire connector.
Add flux to the stripped connectors as specified.
Place the shrink tube over the wires.
Use a 3.18 mm (1/8 inch) shrink tube over the wire-to-wire connectors.
Use a 4.76 mm (3/16 inch) shrink tube over the wire.
Clip the wire-to-wire connector with a “helping hands” tool.
Twist the connector end with the wire.
Solder the twisted connector and wire.
Place a 3.18 mm shrink tube over the soldered connection and shrink it.
Place a 4.76 mm shrink tube over the 3.18 mm shrink tube and shrink it.
Clip the LED wires with tape under them for stability.
Mix epoxy according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Spread the mixed epoxy over the top of the soldered LED.
Leave the epoxy overnight to cure completely.
If mounting using a touch fastener, cut a small piece of the touch fastener.
Press the touch fastener against the back of the LED for 30 seconds.
Use a high-speed rotary tool to make a notch on the lid of a black box.
Drill a 1.75 cm hole through the top of a black box where the LED will be placed.
Using a high-speed rotary tool, make a notch on one side of the drilled hole for wire management.
Cut a piece of privacy film (25–30 mm).
Tape the privacy film onto the inside of the black box covering the hole that the LED will illuminate through.
Place the LED outside the black box on top of the hole with privacy film.
Tape the LED in place with electrical tape.
Drill four 0.83 cm holes on the lid for potentiometers, spaced 3.81 cm apart.
Cut a 1.19 cm x 1.90 cm rectangular hole in the top-left corner of the lid.
Drill a 1.75 cm hole on the black box.
File the drilled holes and insert grommets into them.
Sand the area where the microcontroller will be glued to the black box.
Glue the bottom side of the microcontroller holder and snap the microcontroller onto it.
Epoxy the microcontroller holder in place within the black box.
Sandpaper the bottom of two clips.
Secure the clips inside the black box with epoxy.
Place the PCB board into the secured clips.
Push the power switch through a square hole on the lid and snap it into place.
Push the POTs through the holes on the lid.
Screw the POTs into place.
Put the knob onto each POT.
Label the wire-to-wire connectors (e.g., LED, POT, COM).
Attach the crimped connectors to the male wire-to-wire connector between the two female connectors (POT and LED).
Connect the crimped ends into the microcontroller.
Pull the USB cable through the grommet.
Plug the USB cable into the microcontroller.
Pull the wires for the LEDs through the grommet.
Connect the LED wires to the female wire-to-wire connector on the left of the microcontroller connection.
Pull the wire for the power supply through the grommet.
Connect the power supply wire to the male wire-to-wire connector on the right side of the PCB board.
Connect the male wire-to-wire connector from the power switch to the female wire-to-wire connector on the right of the PCB board.
Connect the male wire-to-wire connectors from the POTs on the lid to the female wire-to-wire connectors on the PCB board.
Plate HEK293 cells at 100k cells per well in a 24-well plate.
Transfect HEK293 cells using serum-free media, Polyethylenimine (PEI), and DNA volumes as calculated from the example table.
Handle transfected cells in the dark or under non-exciting light conditions.
Decide on the type of light stimulation to use for the cells.
Turn off the POTs by turning them counterclockwise.
Turn on the LED power supply.
Place a light meter inside the black box where the cells will be placed and place the lid with the LEDs over the meter.
Adjust the light intensity as needed.
Connect the user interface software to the microcontroller via the selected COM port.
Prepare luciferase reagent by mixing 10 mL of luciferase buffer with luciferase reagent and aliquot in 1 mL tubes to be stored at -80°C for up to 1 year.
Prepare lysis buffer 5x into 1x for N + 2 wells, e.g., for 30 samples, add 30 x 20 µL of 5X lysis buffer and 30 x 80 µL of MQ H2O.
Prepare Renilla substrate solution: mix 20 µL of Renilla substrate with 1 mL of Renilla buffer (suitable for 10 assays).
Remove cells from the incubator, aspirate the media, add 100 µL of 1x lysis buffer per well and place it on a shaker at 100 RPM for 15 min.
Place lysates in -20°C for at least 1 h.
Add 100 μL of luciferase reagent per sample into a well of a white 96-well plate.
Set up the plate reader for luminescence, with integration set to 1 s.
Thaw lysates and add them in wells below the luciferase reagent.
Mix 20 µL of sample with luciferase reagent using a multichannel pipette.
Measure luminescence immediately after mixing.
Add 100 µL of Renilla substrate solution.
Scan again after readings plateau.
Divide the Luciferase signal by the Renilla signal to account for transfection efficiency.
Compare luciferase signals normalized for transfection efficiency.
